messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT [P1] prefix-cache miss spike on hosted-api -> elevated latencies and 5xxs for some tenants. paging @amber_oncall. dashboard: https://dash.redwood/INC-4621 

amber_oncall: acked. oncall taking. linking SRE + runtime. collecting initial metrics and logs.

ryan.eng: seeing prefix hit-rate drop ~98% -> ~54% starting at ~09:13 UTC. tail latency to token path jumped 600ms -> 2200ms, errors +4% for affected routes.

maria_sre: quick paste of cache logs (excerpt):
```
[09:12:59] prefix_create prefix=org_123/model-x ctx_len=256 ttl=0
[09:13:11] eviction shard=12 prefix=org_123/model-x reason=ttl_zeroed
[09:13:13] prefix_lookup miss key=org_123/model-x/seq:0 shard=12
[09:13:14] rewarm_start prefix=org_123/model-x fanout=512
[09:13:14] eviction shard=12 prefix=org_123/model-x reason=overcommitted
```

ryan.eng: hypothesis 1: recent config rollout may have set default_ttl=0 for legacy prefixes -> immediate ttl-based evictions. hypothesis 2: rewarm fan-out amplified pressure causing eviction/reinsert churn.

sara_runtime: i'm going to rollback the prefix-config rollout (deploy-id deploy-2026-03-15-0910). will coordinate with deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated: deploy-2026-03-15-0910 -> deploy-2026-03-15-0830 triggered by @sara_runtime. ETA ~2m.

amber_oncall: mitigation notes: enabled temporary sticky caching (enable_prefix_sticky=true) for the hottest prefixes and throttled rewarm concurrency to 10 workers. applying a temporary min-ttl override (min_prefix_ttl=30s) via runtime flags.

ryan.eng: linking hit-rate graph: https://metrics.redwood/prefix_hitrate?range=30m (look at org_123 cluster). you can see the steep drop at 09:13 and partial recovery starting 09:20.

maria_sre: request: please drop per-shard eviction counters and full rewarm logs here. also need list of prefixes created in the last 30m and the exact config change diff for deploy-2026-03-15-0910.

ryan.eng: grep commands to extract local logs:```
kubectl -n prod logs -l app=prefix-cache --since=40m | egrep "eviction|prefix_create|rewarm" > /tmp/evict-tail.log
```

sara_runtime: attaching commit diff: https://repo.redwood/prefix-cache/commit/7a1b2c - introduced `default_ttl` param, default=0 for backward compat. missed guard for legacy prefixes.

maria_sre: assembled quick timeline: 09:11 - config rollout (deploy-2026-03-15-0910) touches prefix-cache default_ttl; 09:13 - eviction storm starts (sharp increase in evictions/shard 10-15); 09:14 - prefix hit-rate collapse; 09:15 - customer error spike and latency SLO breaches; 09:19 - mitigation flags toggled (min-ttl + throttle); 09:22 - partial hit-rate recovery; 09:30 - rollback complete; 09:34 - metrics trending toward normal.

ryan.eng: additional observation: rewarm service faned out ~500 workers at 09:13 to re-populate prefixes, causing huge write pressure and immediate subsequent evictions. logs show repeated insert->evict cycles for same key(s).

maria_sre: digging into shard-mapping: noticed ~3% of prefixes were hashed to unexpected shard ids right after rollout. possible race in shard mapping codepath where alias prefixes (legacy) map to same shard id due to a new hash seed change in commit 7a1b2c. that would amplify eviction pressure on a subset of shards.

ryan.eng: putting this together -> root cause (current hypothesis): simultaneous config change that defaulted TTL=0 + a rewarm fanout race -> immediate ttl-based evictions. a secondary bug in shard hashing during the rollout caused aliasing of several hot prefixes onto a few shards, concentrating pressure and causing thrash and KV reuse anomalies. result: high miss-rate, rewarm storm, intermittent stale KV reads and 5xxs.

amber_oncall: customer impact: three enterprise customers (org_123, org_456, org_789) saw degraded responses for ~8-12 minutes each, partial SLO breach recorded. CS alerted.

sara_runtime: follow-up mitigation steps (short-term):
- enforce min_prefix_ttl=30s in runtime config (done)
- limit rewarm concurrency to 10 (done)
- rollback config rollout to stable (in progress)

maria_sre: long-term actions proposed:
- patch: require explicit non-zero ttl for new prefixes or skip legacy prefixes unless opt-in (PR queued)
- fix: revert unintended hash-seed change; add deterministic canary across shards (PR open)
- add alert: shard_eviction_rate > X for 1m -> trigger automatic rewarm backoff
- add test: simulate rewarm fanout with zero-ttl to validate safety

ryan.eng: code links: PR#312 (min-ttl guard) https://repo.redwood/prefix-cache/pull/312, PR#313 (shard-hash revert) https://repo.redwood/prefix-cache/pull/313. I'm owning the postmortem writeup (will include timeline + graphs).

amber_oncall: handoff: i'm passing to night SRE @maria_sre at 09:45 UTC. please keep this thread for logs/timeline/hypothesis tracking. i'll update zoom bridge notes and customer update.

maria_sre: ack and taking ownership for post-incident timeline and RCA. next steps: collect per-shard counters for last 48h, attach raw evict logs, confirm list of affected prefixes, and verify patch rollout plan.

ryan.eng: quick numeric: estimated excess cost due to rewarm ~0.5 GPU-hours, and impact window ~12 minutes. will mark billing/credits for affected customers after RCA.

deploy-bot: rollback completed: deploy-2026-03-15-0910 -> stable deploy-2026-03-15-0830 by @sara_runtime.

log-bot: archived logs to s3://redwood-incidents/INC-4621/evictions.tar.gz (sha256: a3f5...).

amber_oncall: closing notes: incident mitigated at ~09:34 UTC after throttles + min-ttl + rollback. primary owner: @ryan.eng (RCA + postmortem), secondary: @maria_sre (data collection + monitoring).

maria_sre: action items (tracked): [A] enforce min-ttl + validation (owner: runtime) [B] revert hash-seed change + test (owner: eng-ml/runtime) [C] add shard evict alert + rewarm backoff (owner: eng-sre) [D] customer comms draft (owner: CS).

ryan.eng: i'll produce the postmortem doc and ping product + cs. thanks all for quick response. :heartpulse:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED [P1 -> mitigated] at 1765433960.
